title: The Tool Interface — Why Agents Need Structured I/O

questions.question: An LLM with no tools cannot reliably answer 'what is the weather in Bengaluru right now'. Why?
options: It cannot read a JSON schema, so the provider rejects its tool payloads
Weather data is filtered out of most providers' training corpora
The host never re-invokes it, so its first answer is always the final one
It can only emit text tokens, so it has no way to act on the world
questions.explanation: The output surface of a bare language model is a distribution over next tokens. It can describe an action but cannot take one; the tool interface is what closes that gap.

questions.question: In the loop describe → decide → execute → observe, which step is owned by the model?
options: describe
execute
decide
observe
questions.explanation: The host describes tools, executes calls, and observes results. Only decide is the model's: it answers, calls one or more tools, or refuses.

questions.question: What is the `id` field on a tool call for?
options: Passing the argument object that the executor will receive at run time
Bounding how many times the host may re-run the same tool before it stops
Choosing which of the registered tools the host should run on this turn
Correlating a result with its call when parallel calls return out of order
questions.explanation: name says which tool, arguments says how to call it, id says which call this is. Parallel calls are not guaranteed to return in order, and nothing in an {sum: 42} payload identifies its originating call.

questions.question: A tool argument can hold any city on earth and cannot be enumerated. Which schema choice fits?
options: Declare it as an open string, with the guidance in the description
Declare it with an enum listing the cities the executor supports
Set additionalProperties to false on the enclosing argument object
Mark it as required so the model always has to supply a value for it
questions.explanation: An enum is a hard gate enforced by the validator, not a hint. Constrain a field only when you can enumerate its legal values; otherwise keep it an open string and teach selection in the description.

questions.question: Which statement about pure and consequential tools is correct?
options: Pure tools must be confirmed by the user before every speculative call the host makes
Pure tools are read-only and safe to re-run; consequential tools must be gated
Consequential tools are the ones whose outputs are too large for one context window
A tool counts as consequential only when it can move money within a single turn
questions.explanation: Pure vs consequential is about whether the tool mutates the world. read_file is itself pure — it never mutates anything — even though its output can be sensitive, which is a separate axis.

questions.question: Why does native function calling beat prompting the model to reply in JSON?
options: It lets the model invoke tools without the host having to run any executor code
The call shape is trained in and constrained-decoded, so it validates out of band
It shrinks the system prompt, so every turn costs noticeably fewer input tokens
It removes the need to declare a JSON schema for each tool the model may choose
questions.explanation: Free-text JSON fails 5-15% of the time on frontier models. Native calling trains the exact shape (98-99% valid in strict mode) and puts the payload in its own protocol slot, so it cannot leak into the user-visible reply and always validates.
